newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher on fund buying, spillover.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher on fund buying, spillover.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled higher on a mix of bullish input, including fund buying in the July contract and spillover support from CBOT soybeans, traders said.
Fund buying and concern about possible cold weather damage boosted the July contract to close up eight cents per bushel at $3.84 -- its highest close since Sept 27, 1996, when it settled at $3.88.
Traders had mixed views on the possibility of damage to the HRW wheat crop as a result of cold weather due later Friday in the central U.S. Plains.

Some said wheat emerging from dormancy in northern Oklahoma could be at risk, but other traders disagreed, saying that most of the wheat in Oklahoma and Kansas was not mature enough to be damaged by cold temperatures.

Wheat also drew support from CBOT soybeans, which rallied to close sharply higher on ideas Brazil will impose an export tax on soybeans. Spillover strength also came after more snow fell in the northern Plains, raising the chance of possible flood-related delays in planting U.S. spring wheat.
KCBT wheat settled 4-1/2 to 11 cents higher, with May up 6-1/2 cents at $4.15. March gained 11 cents to close at $4.51.
Traders said E.D. & F. Man International's purchase of 3.7 million July bushels was likely fund-related. Benson-Quinn was an early buyer of July, picking up 1.5 million bushels.
